steps.prompt: A candle is $20$ cm tall and burns down $2$ cm every hour. What would a graph of its height over time look like?

cards.title: Slope and intercept
cards.body: In $y = mx + b$, the slope $m$ is how much $y$ changes when $x$ goes up by $1$, and $b$ is the value of $y$ when $x = 0$ (the $y$-intercept). The slope through two points is $m = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}$. In a real situation, $m$ is the rate and $b$ the starting amount.

cards.title: Worked example: the line through two points
cards.problem: Find the equation of the line through $(2, 5)$ and $(6, 13)$.

steps.text: Slope: the change in $y$ over the change in $x$.
Put a point into $y = 2x + b$: $5 = 2(2) + b$.
So the line is $y = 2x + 1$. Check the other point: $2(6) + 1 = 13$ ✓.

cards.title: Worked example: reading a model
cards.problem: The value $V$, in dollars, of a laptop $t$ years after it was bought is $V = 1200 - 150t$. What do $1200$ and $150$ mean, and when is it worth $\$450$?

steps.text: $1200$ is the value at $t = 0$, the price paid. $150$ is how much value it loses each year.
After $5$ years the laptop is worth $\$450$.

cards.title: Parallel and perpendicular lines
cards.body: Parallel lines have the same slope. Perpendicular lines have slopes that multiply to $-1$: a line with slope $\frac{2}{3}$ is perpendicular to one with slope $-\frac{3}{2}$. A horizontal line $y = k$ has slope $0$.

prompts: What does the slope mean in a real situation? Give your own example.
